units: You're not from here, are you?
How are you? — the honest answer
Is it always like this here?

lessons.title: Coffee — yes. Mondays — no.
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say what you like and don’t like — and ask someone to slow down or repeat.

lessons.title: Two hellos
lessons.blurb: By the end you can greet people (formal and informal), say goodbye, introduce yourself and ask someone's name.

lessons.title: PIN codes, prices & phone numbers
lessons.blurb: By the end you can use numbers 0–100, give your age and phone number, and count things (one book, two books).

lessons.title: You're not from here, are you?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say where you're from and your nationality, and use to be (I'm, he isn't, they aren't).

lessons.title: The family group chat
lessons.blurb: By the end you can talk about your family and use my / your / his / her and 's (Anna's mother).

lessons.title: How are you? — the honest answer
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say how you feel, ask How are you?, and give short answers (Yes, I am / No, I'm not).

lessons.title: So… what do you do?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say your job with a or an (I'm a teacher / an engineer) and ask What do you do?

lessons.title: My place (no filter)
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say where you live and what's in your home with there is / there are.

lessons.title: What's in your bag?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say what you have with have got (I've got a phone) and ask Have you got…?

lessons.title: This one or that one?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can point at things with this / that / these / those and say their colour.

lessons.title: It's 7:30 somewhere
lessons.blurb: By the end you can tell the time and say when things happen — at 3 o'clock, in the morning, at night.

lessons.title: Save the date
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say days, months and dates — on Monday, in July, the third of May — and ask What's the date?

lessons.title: 5 a.m. club vs. night owls
lessons.blurb: By the end you can talk about your daily routine with Present Simple — I get up at 7, she works in a shop.

lessons.title: Always? Sometimes? Never.
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say how often you do things — always / usually / sometimes / never — and ask Do you…? / How often…?

lessons.title: Who, what, when, where, why
lessons.blurb: By the end you can ask questions with Wh- words — What…? Where…? When…? Who…? Why…? How…?

lessons.title: Hidden talents
lessons.blurb: By the end you can say what you can and can't do — I can swim, I can't drive — and ask Can you…?

lessons.title: People-watching
lessons.blurb: By the end you can describe people — She has long hair, He's tall — and use adjectives in order (a tall young man).

lessons.title: Free time, honestly
lessons.blurb: By the end you can talk about hobbies with like / love / hate + -ing — I love dancing, I hate cooking.

lessons.title: Ordering like a local
lessons.blurb: By the end you can order in a café — I'd like a coffee, please — and use some / any with food and drink.

lessons.title: How much is it?!
lessons.blurb: By the end you can shop — ask How much is it? / How many…? and understand prices.

lessons.title: Is it always like this here?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can talk about the weather — It's sunny, It's raining — with Present Continuous.

lessons.title: Let's do something
lessons.blurb: By the end you can invite people — Let's go!, Do you want to…?, Would you like to…? — and say yes or no nicely.

lessons.title: Where were you in 2010?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can talk about the past with was / were — I was at school, they were happy — and ask Where were you?

lessons.title: What did you do?
lessons.blurb: By the end you can make small talk and tell a short first story about the past — I played football, I went to the park, it was fun.
